narrative.overview: Prominentz looks like a ledger book worked late on a busy floor: a mostly black-and-white operational surface — midblack (#0b0b0c, ~60% of any screen) and pure white (#ffffff, ~30%) — with one deliberate mark of violet (#6835F9, ~10%) reserved for the thing that's actually live or actionable right now. Nothing about it should read as decorative; every accent use is a signal, not a flourish. The system was built to be read correctly by someone mid-shift, not admired at rest — precise and unshakeable rather than warm or playful. The system explicitly rejects gradient text, glow effects, and multi-hue decoration. A prior pass had the primary accent faked via background-clip: text on hero copy even where the underlying value was a single flat color — that's been corrected to a plain color assignment; gradients-as-decoration have no place here.
keyCharacteristics: Mostly monochrome (black/white), with a single reserved accent color used sparingly
Real, layered drop shadows for depth (not flat/tonal) — confirmed as the standard, not legacy
Crisp, unambiguous component states: color changes, not soft/ambiguous affordances
Dense, operational typography (Space Grotesk display, Inter body, JetBrains Mono for labels/mono contexts)
Same accent and ink pairing holds in both dark and light mode

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Violet is the only accent color in the system. It appears only on primary buttons, active/selected state, and focus rings — never as a secondary decorative color, never doubled up with another accent. Does not apply to the Operational palette, which is real product status color, not decoration. Governs the app world only; the marketing world has no brand accent.

rules.name: The Weight-Over-Glow Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from shadow weight and layering, never from a colored glow except as a deliberate, sparing focus-ring treatment on the violet accent itself. Don't add decorative glow to anything else.

rules.name: The Two-Scale Rule
rules.body: Inside the app, branded surfaces use the --text-* rem scale; operational/POS/KDS/dashboard surfaces use the px-based Operational Scale. Don't mix them on the same screen, and don't "fix" one by converting it to the other. The public site uses neither; it has its own marketing scale below.

rules.name: The Three Signals Rule
rules.body: On the public site, color means state: blue is now, green is done, orange is late. There is no decorative accent and no violet. If a color does not answer "what state is this in?", it is ink or a ground.

rules.name: The Text Shade Rule
rules.body: A signal color at full strength is a fill, dot, border or ring. When the signal has to be read as text on white or paper, use its derived text shade (site-live-text, site-good-text, site-late-text, site-live-emphasis), which clear 4.5:1.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Marketing headings are sentence case. src/app/globals.css sets every h1–h6 to Barlow Condensed 800 uppercase for the app; every marketing heading class must re-declare font-family, font-weight and text-transform: none (as .h1, .h2, .h3 do). Never use a bare h1–h6 on a marketing page without one of the site's type classes.

rules.name: The Label Lives In The Panel Rule
rules.body: The mono uppercase label is product chrome: it appears inside panels, bills, tables and the tracker, describing the data beside it. It never sits above a section headline as a kicker or eyebrow.

rules.name: The One Lift Rule
rules.body: Only product panels are lifted. Tier cards, seat cards, tickets and fields sit flat with a hairline.

dos: Do keep violet (#6835F9) reserved for primary actions and active/focus state only — never decorative.
Do use Ledger Black (#0b0b0c) as the dark-mode ground and the light-mode ink; don't introduce a second "almost black."
Do keep real layered box-shadows for elevation in both themes — this system is not flat/tonal.
Do use white text on violet backgrounds, and --brand-text (not --brand) when violet is the text color itself — it switches to #a78bfa in dark mode for contrast.
Do (marketing) take every color on the public site from a ground class (.dark, .light, .paper) and the site-* tokens, so components work on any ground.
Do (marketing) show the product through demo panels in site tokens, with a mono label in the panel head.
Do (marketing) use the signal text shades (#5b28ee, #1a8a4e, #b91c1c, #5b28ee) whenever a signal color is read as text on white or paper.
Do (marketing) give every marketing heading a site type class that resets the global uppercase Barlow rule.
Do (marketing) keep the static fallback complete: anything shown in the theatre must also render in the stacked story.
donts: Don't fake colored text with background-clip: text / gradient tricks — set color directly. (Already corrected once this session; don't reintroduce it.)
Don't add a second accent color alongside violet on the same app screen.
Don't soften button/input radii below the md (6px) step — it reads as off-brand "soft SaaS," not this system's operational character.
Don't let sidebar/nav "current" states borrow the violet accent — that's reserved for actions, not location indicators.
Don't import app CSS classes or --brand/--color-* variables into the site, or site-* tokens into the app; the values match since 2026-11-14, the composition does not.
Don't (marketing) use live, good or late as decoration; each means a state.
Don't (marketing) put the mono label above a section headline as a kicker or eyebrow.
Don't (marketing) set ink text on violet or white text on green or amber; white goes on violet and red, ink goes on green and amber.

marketing.overview: The public site tells one dinner order, Table 12's, from the seat to the close of day, in the app's own clothes (Direction C). Graphite signage (site-ground-dark) opens and closes the story; the service in between happens on back-office grey (site-ground-light, with white site-paper for alternating bands). Violet (site-live) is the only action color and marks what is happening now; status is a solid block with a word: green ready, amber cooking, red late. The product is the illustration: every visual is a working demo panel rendered in the same tokens the app uses, a white card with hairlines, 8px corners, a soft shadow and a mono label on top. On wide screens with motion allowed, the story plays as a scroll theatre; everywhere else it reads as a stacked sequence with the same content.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite stage, grey back-office scenes, one ink; the topbar flips with the ground under it
Three meaningful signals (live, good, late); no brand accent color on the site
Funnel Display headlines in sentence case, Inter body, Roboto Mono for tickets, times, prices and panel labels
Product panels instead of illustration, mockup or feature-card grids
Scroll theatre with a static fallback that loses nothing
